connector: Lucy had tea with a Faun! But when she comes back, the others don’t believe her. Today you read Chapters 2 and 3. Notice how Narnia feels inside Mr. Tumnus’s warm cave, and how different it feels when Edmund steps through.

a.raw: the dwarf cracked his whip and the bells on the sledge jingled
a.fixed: The dwarf cracked his whip, and the bells on the sledge jingled.
a.why: The starts the sentence. A comma goes before and, because and joins two complete thoughts. A period ends it.

b.raw: the queen wore a golden crown and she held a long golden wand
b.fixed: The Queen wore a golden crown, and she held a long golden wand.
b.why: The starts the sentence. Queen gets a capital because it is used as her name. A comma goes before and. A period ends it.

cards.title: World Notes: Fauns in Old Stories
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapters with your lens in mind.
text: Fauns come from very old stories told in ancient Rome, about 2,000 years ago.
Stories say a faun is half person and half goat, with goat legs and small horns, and lives in the woods.
Lewis borrowed the faun from those old stories and made Mr. Tumnus.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Lucy is back, and nobody believes her. Today, notice how Narnia feels in a warm cave, and in a cold, quiet wood.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: match tele words, find connecting words, and spot the lazy uh.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapters 2 and 3. Then try my video in Read Like a Writer.
transcripts.guide3: Today you write the opening sentence of your literary response.

notes.wordParts: The word part tele means far. telephone = sound from far away. telescope = a tool for looking far away.
notes.grammar: A complex sentence has a main idea and a part that cannot stand alone, joined by a word like when, because or although. When that part comes first, put a comma after it.
notes.spelling: The schwa is a lazy uh sound in a quiet beat of a long word. Any vowel can make it: the a in sofa, the e in seven, the o in lemon.
notes.wgrd: A setting can change with the mood: Mr. Tumnus’s cave feels warm and cozy, and the empty wood feels cold and still.
vocab: eager to find out; very curious
a deep feeling of sadness or gloom
strange or unusual in a hard-to-explain way
to be disloyal to someone who trusted you

plate.alt: An old painting of hunters and their dogs walking down a snowy hill above a village, with people skating on frozen ponds below
plate.credit: The Hunters in the Snow · Pieter Bruegel the Elder, 1565 · Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna · Public domain
plate.look: A painting by Pieter Bruegel, made in 1565, more than 450 years ago. Hunters and their dogs trudge home through deep snow. Down below, people skate on frozen ponds. Every roof is white. Bruegel shows how winter changes a whole world, just as Lewis does in Narnia.
plate.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this painting of hunters in the snow

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. A setting can change with the mood. A warm cave with a fire feels very different from a cold, quiet wood. Notice how each place makes you feel. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. The Queen told the dwarf to stop, and Edmund stared at her golden crown. Queen gets a capital, because it's used as her name. And there's that comma before and again. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Read the poem out loud. Then answer the question.
mods.script: [curious] Here's a poem by William Blake, written more than two hundred years ago. Read it out loud. Blake talks right to the tiger, as if it could listen and answer him. That's personification. Then answer the question: what is Blake asking the tiger?

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap what it means. Match all four words.
mods.script: Watch one match first. Find tele, and remember: it means far. Telework. Tele, far. Work. Telework means working far from the office, like at home. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four words.
mods.script: Here's another word from Chapter 1. Glimpse. Lucy could even catch a glimpse of the empty room. Just a quick look, through the trees. So a glimpse is a quick look. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.

mods.todo: Find the connecting words. Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap every word that is wrong.
mods.script: Spot the connecting word. Because it was raining, the children explored the house. Because! It starts the part that can't stand alone. Find the connecting word in each sentence, and tap Now check your thinking. Then fix the paragraph. Read slowly: the mistakes aren't all the same kind.

mods.todo: Read the rule. Tap every word with a lazy schwa beat.
mods.script: Lazy beat hunt! Susan pulled the coats apart. Susan. Soo, zun. A lazy beat, yes! Pulled? Just one beat, no. Apart. Uh, part. Yes! Read the rule. Then tap every word with a schwa in the two sentences.

mods.todo: Read Chapters 2 and 3 in your book. Then try the Truth Watch below.
mods.script: Read Chapters 2 and 3 in your book, with your lens in mind. Then try the Truth Watch, and watch my video in the Read Like a Writer box before you write.

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.script: [warmly] Let's try all three parts with a different sentence from Chapter 3. There was crisp, dry snow under his feet and more snow lying on the branches of the trees. Part one, read like a reader. Edmund is in Narnia now, and it's winter. Part two, read like a writer. Lewis starts at Edmund's feet, then looks up at the trees, so you look around with him. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: There was cold, wet sand under my feet and more sand stuck to my shoes. Now it's your turn with Lewis's sentence about the house. Write one sentence in each box.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the book.
mods.script: Three questions, in full sentences. One, two details that make Mr. Tumnus's cave cozy. Two, why the others don't believe Lucy. Think about the time, and the back of the wardrobe. Three, how Narnia and the Professor's house feel different.

mods.todo: Write your opening sentence: the book, the author, and what you will show.
mods.script: Today you write one sentence: your opening. Clara's rough try didn't say much. Her new one names the book, the author, and what she will prove. Do the same for yours.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Lucy tells the others she has been away for hours and hours.
items.why: She tells them what really happened to her.

items.t: Edmund taps his head and calls Lucy batty.
items.why: Making fun of someone is not about telling the truth. It hurts Lucy.

items.t: Lucy says, “It wasn’t a hoax at all. Honestly it was. I promise.”
items.why: She keeps telling the truth, even when no one believes her.
